messages.subject: TMT annotations file details
messages.body_plain:
Hi - I have lots of experience running MSstats for LFQ data, but now trying to analyze a TMT dataset.  My experimental design is as follows:

6plex TMT:  6 timepoint series
fractionate samples (16 fractions)
run each fraction in on mass spec

I have 3 biological replicates, each contained within their own 6plex experiment.  I am confused about setting up annotations files:

Run:  Mass spec raw file name.  This is repeated for every channel and every fraction (12 fractions x 6 channels)
Channel:  channel.0 through channel.5
Condition:  My naming for each timepoint
Mixture:  Mixture 1, 2, and 3.  One for each biological replicate set
BioReplicate:  1.X126

When I tried with attached file I get the following error:

> input.mq <http://input.mq/> <- MaxQtoMSstatsTMTFormat(evidence=evidence_df, proteinGroups=pg_df, annotation=anno_df)
** + Contaminant, + Reverse, + Only.identified.by.site, proteins are removed.
** PSMs, that have all zero intensities across channels in each run, are removed.
** 5087 features have 1 or 2 intensities across runs and are removed.
** Multiple measurements in a feature and a run are summarized by summaryforMultipleRows.
** Annotation for Run : QE20150215-03, Channel : channel.6 are missed.
....
And this continues complaining about all subsequent raw files.

Thanks,

-Danielle

messages.subject: Re: TMT annotations file details
messages.body_plain:
Hi Danielle,

Here is the issue with your annotation file:
1. Run:  MS Run ID.  If I understand correctly, there are 3 mixtures by 12 fractions = 36 MS runs in your experiment. Since the data is processed by MaxQuant, Run should be the same as Raw.file info in evidence_df file. Each mixture in Mixture column should correspond to 12 MS runs (One fraction is one MS run).
2. Condition: each timepoint. The way you set it seems correct but please make sure the Condition value is determined by the columns Mixture and Channel.
3.  BioReplicate: same as Mixture in your experiment since there are three biological replicates.

Last, when you run the MaxQuant converter, you need to set the argument fraction = True as follows
input.mq <http://www.google.com/url?q=http%3A%2F%2Finput.mq%2F&sa=D&sntz=1&usg=AFQjCNFn6MZ2qneS0iktGJcmPmLijXWIRw> <- MaxQtoMSstatsTMTFormat(evidence=evidence_df, proteinGroups=pg_df, annotation=anno_df, fraction=True)

Best,
Ting

messages.subject: Re: MSstatsTMT documentation
messages.body_plain:
Hi Tom,

The annotation file for MaxQuant should be prepared as follows:
Run : MS run ID. It should be the same as Raw.file info in the evidence file of MaxQuant
Channel : Labeling information (channel.0, ..., channel.5). The channel index should be consistent with the channel columns in evidence file.
Condition : Condition (ex. Healthy, Cancer)
Mixture : Mixture of samples with different TMT reagents, which can be analyzed in a single mass spectrometry experiment. The mixture may be fractionated into multiple fractions. Then one mixture should correspond to multiple MS runs (One fraction is one MS run). For example, if ’Run’ = 1, 2, 3 are three fractions of one TMT mixture of biological samples, then they should have same ’Mixture’ value.
BioReplicate : Unique ID for biological subject. In your data, there should be only 3 biological replicates.
MSstatsTMT performs normalization after protein summarization based on the reference channel, which are usually the master-pool samples. For each protein, it equalizes the protein intensity in the reference channel across all the MS runs to their median.

We are preparing the manuscript for MSstatsTMT. Later, you may refer to it about the mathematical details .

Best,
Ting

messages.subject: MSStatsTMT proposed vs LIMMA
messages.body_plain:
Hello MSStats developer Team,
I am currently trying to compare "proposed" and "limma" groupcomparisons in the MSStatsTMT package.
I can run the "proposed" method without any problems. However, when I wanted to try out limma I got the following message:

> test.Panc1_OEvsLV_MedianP_LIMMA <- groupComparison.TMT(quant_Panc1, contrast.matrix = contrast_matrix_Panc1, remove_norm_channel = T, model = "limma",
+                                                        adj.method = "BH")
Error in contrasts.fit(fit, contrast.matrix) :
  Number of rows of contrast matrix must match number of coefficients in fit
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In rn != cn :
  longer object length is not a multiple of shorter object length
2: In contrasts.fit(fit, contrast.matrix) :
  row names of contrasts don't match col names of coefficients

Exactly the same contrast matrix and input work fine with both ttest and proposed.
Do I need to change the contrast matrix or the input?

Best Regards and thank you for your great efforts.
Klemens

It seems like the version of MSstatsTMT you are using is not the latest.I would recommend you to install the latest MSstatsTMT from Bioconductor. Several changes are made and some bugs are fixed in that version. One thing you may want to know is that the groupComparisonTMT() function in the latest MSstatsTMT no longer supports "ttest".

Best,
Ting

messages.subject: Re: MSstats is not available for R version 3.5.3
messages.subject_clean: MSstats is not available for R version 3.5.3
messages.body_plain:
Dear Sapir,

I guess that you tried to install MSstats through CRAN, 'install.packages('msstats')'

However, MSstats is available in Bioconductor. Please install MSstats (or MSstatsTMT, MSstatsQC) through bioconductor. Both below should work.

HTH
- Meena

source("http://bioconductor.org/biocLite.R")
biocLite("MSstats")

or

if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("MSstats", version = "3.8")
